advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Narrow the `timeout`/`fallback` failover trigger tokens (e.g. to more specific phrases like `TimeoutError`, `should_fall_back`) to avoid firing on incidental `timeout=`/`read_timeout` substrings.
evidence: criteria_routing.json trigger_tokens include `"timeout"` and `"fallback"` — bare substrings
registry.py:634 `if oid not in fired and any(tok in body for tok in tokens): fired.add(oid)` — literal substring match on any added/removed line body
The overlay is advisory (`blocking_enabled: false`, threshold 0.95), so over-firing costs an extra advisory pass rather than a wrong verdict, but broadens fan-out substantially
advisory.finding: The `timeout` trigger token (and to a lesser degree `fallback`/`retryable`) is a bare, extremely common substring, so `content_triggered_overlays` will fire the failover overlay on a large fraction of unrelated diffs (e.g. any line containing `timeout=`, `read_timeout`, `ConnectTimeout`, `socket.timeout`). This is a precision problem for the content trigger.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a negative-control test that a `failover` trigger token (e.g. `should_fall_back`) on an unchanged context line does NOT fire `failover` via content_triggered_overlays.
evidence: registry.py:638 `_scan_packaged_tokens` is newly added and delegates to the new `_scan_token_map` (registry.py:624)
test_failover_committed_token_fires_on_fallback_diff asserts only the positive firing case (both tokens on `+` lines)

Named violating input: a diff containing `should_fall_back(error)` only on a space-prefixed CONTEXT line (e.g. `--- a/x.py
+++ b/x.py
@@ -1,2 +1,2 @@
     if should_fall_back(error):
+    pass
`) must NOT fire `failover`; no test covers this on the packaged-scanner path
ABSENCE rationale: the concurrency context-line negative control at test_code_review_triggers.py:197 exercises `_has_concurrency_token`, not `_scan_token_map`, so it does not guard the new scanner
advisory.finding: The newly added generic packaged-token scanner `_scan_packaged_tokens` / `_scan_token_map` has a positive firing test but no negative control asserting a trigger token appearing only on an UNCHANGED context (space-prefixed) diff line does NOT fire the overlay. The existing context-line negative control (test_context_line_only_token_does_not_fire_concurrency) exercises `_has_concurrency_token`, a separate code path, so the new scanner's `+`/`-` prefix gating (registry.py:628-631) is unverified for the failover/packaged route.
scenarios: A future edit to `_scan_token_map`'s line-prefix filter would silently over-fire packaged overlays on context lines with no failing test on the failover path
